text: For years, no one knew what made them.
One: a giant shark. Two: a parasite. Three: a fish shorter than your arm.
It's number three: the cookiecutter shark.
It latches on with suction-cup lips, sinks in its teeth, then spins its whole body to carve out a round plug.
It even bit the rubber sonar domes of U.S. Navy submarines.
And its belly glows in the dark.
